q1_issues.issue: A scalar-change subject takes Theme, not Patient.

The delta rides the generic Measure head instead of MeasureBy, and its scale is the verb lemma 'rise'; the dimension noun the clause actually supplies is 'rate' (a scale no word supplies is never invented).
'to 6.1%' is stored as the bearer's own timeless (Measure sk_rate_1 level 6.1 percent), which the scalar-change rule explicitly forbids — an end value must be MeasureTo on the event.

(Most high sk_rate_1 level) drops 'since July 1994', widening it to an all-time high; it also predicates the superlative of the rate entity rather than of the value, and the required companion (Member sk_rate_1 level) is missing.

q2_gaps: a superlative restricted by a temporal window ('the highest level since July 1994') — Most has no slot for the comparison window
an appositive renaming a measured VALUE rather than an entity ('to 6.1%, the highest level ...') — there is no symbol for the value to host the appositive typing
notes: The rate compound plus genus, the rise event and its Past are right, and both figures are recorded with correct magnitudes and units; every defect is in which head or bearer carries them.
